published_statement: AS CAPTURED BY THE TREE (not re-read here): eq. (2.8), printed p.6: 'In the electroweak theory, the tunneling probability is unobservably small, Gamma_inst ~ exp(-4 pi / alpha_W) ~ 10^-170, (2.8) where alpha_W = g^2/4 pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29'. Sec. 2 p.5: 'At zero energies and temperatures, the transition between vacua with different n[omega] is a tunnelling event which is described by instantons' ... 'In pure Yang-Mills theory an instanton is the solution to the Euclidean field equations'. Sec. 4.1 p.11: 'This process can be described by instantons and is strongly suppressed by the semiclassical exponent exp(-4 pi / alpha_W).' Sec. 2 eqs (2.2)-(2.4): 'Delta N_F^(i) = N[A]', with 'Delta N_e = Delta N_mu = Delta N_tau = (1/3) Delta B ; (B - L) is conserved while (B + L) is violated'.
published_hypotheses: H1 zero energy and zero temperature (T = 0, E = 0): the vacuum-to-vacuum transition is a tunnelling event (captured, Sec. 2 p.5)

H2 semiclassical / weak-coupling (WKB) approximation: probability ~ exp(-2 S_inst), S_inst = 8 pi^2/g^2 (the form the exponent implies; the capture holds only the exponent and 'semiclassical exponent', Sec. 4.1)
H3 exponent only, the '~' of eq. (2.8): no pre-exponential factor is given in the captured text
H4 the instanton is an exact solution 'in pure Yang-Mills theory' (captured, p.5); in the gauge-Higgs theory it is not (the constrained-instanton setting) -- the source's own qualifier, as captured
H5 coupling: alpha_W = g^2/4 pi = alpha/sin^2 theta_W = 1/29 (eq. (2.8), captured); scheme and scale of alpha and sin^2 theta_W not stated in the captured text
H6 selection rule: Delta B = Delta L = N_f (x Delta N_CS), B - L conserved (eqs (2.2)-(2.4), captured)
H7 data of 1996: m_W ~ 80.3 GeV, sin^2 theta_W ~ 0.23, m_t measured (1995), m_H unknown (discovered 2012) -- context from general knowledge, not read at source
hypothesis_drift: UNNAMED SCHEME/SCALE OF alpha_W (weakened hypothesis H5) -- massform.py:527-531 names 'alpha_W = g^2/4 pi, with g = 2 m_W/v' (tree-level, G_F) and prints 10^-160.95 to two decimals and 'attempts x prefactor >= 10^189.10' (massform.py:532-533); it does not name that at leading order the choice of scheme/scale for alpha_W is a convention fixed only at next order (the prefactor). COMPUTED here: d log10/d(1/alpha_W) = 5.4575 decades per unit; the definitions in use give 1/alpha_W from 29.49 (G_F tree) and 29.59 (MS-bar at M_Z) to 30.59 (on-shell with alpha(0)) and 31.73 (alpha(0)/sin^2_eff), i.e. 10^-160.95 .. 10^-173.16 -- about 12 decades of convention (inputs other than the tree's RECALLED, not read here). The conclusion is untouched: every scheme leaves the suppression below 10^-158; the 10^189.10 threshold rises under each of the four conventions listed (each gives a smaller alpha_W) and falls only under the source's own 1/29, to 10^186.41 (2.68 decades).

DROPPED H4 (pure-Yang-Mills qualifier / constrained instanton) -- massform.py:524-533 carries the source's T=0 sentence but not its 'In pure Yang-Mills theory' qualifier (which the tree holds only in the SOURCES locator string, massform.py:1076-1077). Harmless in direction, COMPUTED here: the Bogomolny identity sum(F -+ Ftilde)^2 = 2F^2 -+ 2F Ftilde (machine-checked for a generic field) gives S_gauge >= 8 pi^2 |Q|/g^2, and the Higgs terms are non-negative, so every Q = 1 Euclidean path in the gauge-Higgs theory has S_E >= 8 pi^2/g^2: the Higgs can only deepen the suppression the tree uses.
H3 KEPT, NOT DRIFTED -- massform.py:531-532 'No prefactor was read, so NO RATE IS PRINTED' matches the '~' of eq. (2.8); the canonical entry's hypothesis 'no prefactor read' is faithful.

COUPLING SUBSTITUTED AND DECLARED -- massform.py:527-531 replaces the source's 1/29 by 1/29.49 from m_W (PDG-2026 capture) and v (G_F, NAMED-NOT-READ) and says so ('INHERITS NAMED-NOT-READ through v'); 'exactly as the source states it' (massform.py:530) refers to the functional form exp(-4 pi/alpha_W) = exp(-16 pi^2/g^2), not to the number -- not a drift.

lacked_data: What the authors lacked in 1996: the Higgs mass (2012), a precise m_W (+/- ~0.1 GeV then vs ~0.01 now), and the post-LEP-II electroweak fits. EVIDENCE THAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION, all COMPUTED here: (a) the leading exponent 8 pi^2/g^2 is a property of the self-dual BPST solution and, by the Bogomolny bound, a lower bound on the Euclidean action of every Q = 1 gauge-Higgs path -- it contains neither m_H nor m_t, so the missing Higgs mass cannot lift the suppression, only deepen it through the constrained-instanton term; (b) the m_W move 1996 -> 2026 shifts the exponent by < 0.1 decade; (c) the authors' 1/29 vs today's 1/29.49 (tree inputs) is 2.68 decades, and the whole convention band is ~15 decades, against a suppression of ~160 decades. EVIDENCE THE OTHER WAY: none found for the T = 0 exponent. Where data genuinely matter is the prefactor (m_H-dependent, unread by the tree) and the high-energy collider rate, which the tree already holds CONTESTED in S11. M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result on the computable legs; the source itself could not be read in this stage, so that verdict rests on the tree's captures plus the re-derivation, not on the page.
